Description

PGE2 formed in the inflamed joint binds the EP1 receptor, which about a third of sensory neurons express. EP1 couples to Gq, whose α subunit activates phospholipase Cβ. In sensory neurons this pathway sensitises TRPV1 through protein kinase C and lowers its heat threshold, and it enhances calcium entry through store-operated Orai1 channels. Mice lacking EP1 show less PGE2-induced allodynia and inflammatory heat hyperalgesia. RGS proteins end Gq signalling by accelerating GTP hydrolysis. The role of EP1 in osteoarthritis pain is inferred from these inflammatory pain models, while blocking EP4 relieves pain in an osteoarthritis model.

Colour

Proteins and metabolites are coloured by their contribution to pain: red for those that raise it (they excite or sensitise nociceptive neurons, or drive the inflammation that does), blue for those that relieve it, and olive for the shared signalling machinery (G proteins, RGS, adenylate cyclase, phospholipases, kinases, adaptors, second messengers, ions and nucleotides), whose effect is set by the receptor upstream. Metabolites take a lighter shade of the same colour. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white. Each molecule is coloured by its role in this block, so the same molecule can be red in one block and blue in another.

PGE2 and EP1 are red: EP1 raises calcium in nociceptors through Gq and phospholipase C.
